dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:5601.text: A large head. Formed from 頁, with 石 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5602.text: A large head. Formed from 頁, with 分 indicating the sound. Another explanation: temple hair. The Odes says: “Large is its head.”

shuowen:5603.text: A large head. Formed from 頁, with 禺 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Its size is grand.”

shuowen:5604.text: A large head. Formed from 頁, with 羔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5605.text: A large head. Formed from 頁, with 骨 indicating the sound. Read like 魁.

shuowen:5606.text: A large head. Formed from 頁, with 原 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5607.text: A high, long head. Formed from 頁, with 堯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5608.text: 𩕀顤, high. Formed from 頁, with 敖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5609.text: The front of the face prominent and lofty, 岳岳. Formed from 頁, with 岳 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5610.text: Obscured in front, 昧前; the gloss is uncertain. Formed from 頁, with 𡿯 indicating the sound. Read like 昧.

shuowen:5611.text: The face thin and shallow, 𩖊𩖊. Formed from 頁, with 霝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5612.text: The head covered, 𩔀; the repeated gloss is uncertain. Formed from 頁, with 㒸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5613.text: A solid, rounded head, 㮯頭; the precise description is uncertain. Formed from 頁, with 元 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5614.text: A small head, 𩓸𩓸. Formed from 頁, with 枝 indicating the sound. Read like 規.

shuowen:5615.text: A small head. Formed from 頁, with 果 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5616.text: A short face. Formed from 頁, with 𠯑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5617.text: A narrow head. Formed from 頁, with 廷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5618.text: The head composed and practiced in bearing. Formed from 頁, with 危 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5619.text: A yellow face. Formed from 頁, with 含 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5620.text: A face not straight. Formed from 頁, with 爰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5621.text: To raise the head. Formed from 頁, with 支 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The cap stands raised.”

shuowen:5622.text: To put the head into water. Formed from 頁 and 𠬸; 𠬸 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5623.text: To turn and look back. Formed from 頁, with 雇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5624.text: Orderly or in accord. Formed from 頁 and 巛.

shuowen:5625.text: A 䪾䫰 facial expression, showing care in affairs. Formed from 頁, with 㐱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5626.text: The expression 䪾䫰. Formed from 頁, with 粦 indicating the sound. Another explanation: little hair on the head.

shuowen:5627.text: The head showing a cautious manner, 顓顓. Formed from 頁, with 耑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5628.text: The head showing a cautious manner, 頊頊. Formed from 頁, with 玉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5629.text: To lower the head. Formed from 頁, with 金 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “He welcomed him at the gate and merely nodded.”

shuowen:5630.text: To lower the head. Formed from 頁, with 屯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5631.text: To lower the head. Formed from 頁 and abbreviated 逃. The Grand Historian’s divination writings use this form for 頫 in “looking down and up.” Yang Xiong says: “A person’s face looks downward.”

shuowen:5632.text: To raise the eyes and look at someone. Formed from 頁, with 臣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5633.text: To look arrogantly at someone. Formed from 頁, with 善 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5634.text: To straighten the neck. Formed from 頁, with 吉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5635.text: The head held upright, 頡䪼. Formed from 頁, with 出 indicating the sound. Also read like 骨.

shuowen:5636.text: A white appearance. Formed from 頁 and 景. The Songs of Chu says: “Heaven is white and bright.” The four Hao of the Southern Mountain were white-headed men.

shuowen:5637.text: An extremely ugly appearance. Formed from 頁, with 樊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5638.text: A handsome appearance. Formed from 頁, with 爭 indicating the sound. This is what the Odes calls a “𩓞 head.”

shuowen:5639.text: A beautiful head. Formed from 頁, with abbreviated 翩 indicating the sound. Read like 翩.

shuowen:5640.text: A cautious, dignified appearance. Formed from 頁, with 豈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5641.text: Little hair on the head and temples. Formed from 頁, with 肩 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “Many eyes and a 顅 neck”; the quoted phrase is uncertain.

shuowen:5642.text: Without hair. Another explanation: the opening of the ear. Formed from 頁, with 囷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5643.text: Bald. Formed from 頁, with 气 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5644.text: The head not upright. Formed from 頁 and 耒; 耒 depicts the head inclined. Also read like 齧 in the Spring and Autumn’s Xia Nie of Chen.

shuowen:5645.text: To incline the head. Formed from 頁, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5646.text: To watch a person. Another explanation: fearful. Formed from 頁, with 契 indicating the sound. Read like 褉.

shuowen:5647.text: The head not upright. Formed from 頁, with 鬼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5648.text: The head tilted to one side. Formed from 頁, with 皮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5649.text: To tremble. Formed from 頁, with 尤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5650.text: The head not upright. Formed from 頁, with 亶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5651.text: Not getting enough food, with a yellow face and lines appearing; the wording 起行 is uncertain. Formed from 頁, with 咸 indicating the sound. Read like 戇.

shuowen:5652.text: The face gaunt or discolored, 䫲顲; the precise expression is uncertain. Formed from 頁, with 𤎭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5653.text: A feverish headache. Formed from 頁 and 火. Another explanation: abbreviated 焚 indicates the sound.

shuowen:5654.text: Foolish, neither perceptive nor clear-minded. Formed from 頁, with 𧱏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5655.text: Hard to understand. Formed from 頁 and 米. Another explanation: a fresh white appearance, using abbreviated 粉.

shuowen:5656.text: Haggard, 顦顇. Formed from 頁, with 焦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5657.text: Haggard, 顦顇. Formed from 頁, with 卒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5658.text: The head constricted and faint, 繫頭殟; the gloss is uncertain. Formed from 頁, with 昏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5659.text: Ugly. Formed from 頁, with 亥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5660.text: Ugly. Formed from 頁, with 其 indicating the sound. Present-day expulsion of pestilence uses 䫏 masks.

shuowen:5661.text: To call out. Formed from 頁, with 籥 indicating the sound. Pronounced the same as 籥. The Book of Shang says: “Lead and call together the many relatives.”

shuowen:5662.text: Bright ornament on the head. Formed from 頁, with 㬎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5663.text: To select and equip, 選具; the gloss is uncertain. Formed from two 頁.

shuowen:5664.text: At ease. Note: the classics also use 豫. Formed from 頁; further details are unknown.

shuowen:5665.text: The head. Pictographic. All characters in this group are formed from 𦣻.

shuowen:5666.text: A gentle facial expression. Formed from 𦣻 and 肉. Read like 柔.

shuowen:5667.text: The front of the head. Formed from 𦣻, depicting a person’s face. All characters in this group are formed from 面.

shuowen:5668.text: The face visible. Formed from 面 and 見; 見 also indicates the sound. The Odes says: “Showing that face and those eyes.”

shuowen:5669.text: The cheek. Formed from 面, with 甫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5670.text: The face scorched, withered and small. Formed from 面 and 焦.

shuowen:5671.text: Beauty or graceful appearance. Formed from 面, with 厭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5672.text: Not visible. Depicts obstruction and covering. All characters in this group are formed from 丏.

shuowen:5673.text: The same as 𦣻, the ancient graph 𦣻. 巛 depicts hair, called 鬊; 鬊 is 巛. All characters in the 𩠐 group follow 𩠐.

shuowen:5674.text: To lower the head. Formed from 𩠐, with 旨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5675.text: To pierce, 戳. Formed from 𩠐 and 斷.

shuowen:5676.text: An inverted head. Palace Attendant Jia says this graph means a severed head hung upside down. All characters in this group are formed from 𥄉.

shuowen:5677.text: To suspend. Formed from 系 holding 𥄉.

shuowen:5678.text: Facial hair. Formed from 頁 and 彡. All characters in this group are formed from 須.

shuowen:5679.text: Hair above the mouth. Formed from 須, with 此 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5680.text: Cheek hair. Formed from 須 and 冄; 冄 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5681.text: Beard and hair half white. Formed from 須, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5682.text: The appearance of short beard and hair. Formed from 須, with 否 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5683.text: Hair ornaments and painted patterns. Pictographic. All characters in this group are formed from 彡.

shuowen:5684.text: Shape or representation. Formed from 彡, with 幵 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5685.text: Thick hair. Formed from 彡 and 人. The Odes says: “Thick hair like clouds.”

shuowen:5686.text: To adorn. Formed from 彡, with 攸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5687.text: A pattern made manifest. Formed from 彡 and 章; 章 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5688.text: To carve patterns. Formed from 彡, with 周 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5689.text: Pure or bright ornament. Formed from 彡, with 青 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5690.text: Fine patterns. Formed from 彡, with abbreviated 𡭴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5691.text: Pliant or bent. The upper part depicts bending; 彡 depicts hair’s pliancy and weakness. Weak things occur together, hence two 𢎥.

shuowen:5692.text: Patterned ornament. Formed from 彡, with 采 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5693.text: Patterned or adorned. Formed from 彡 and 文. All characters in this group are formed from 彣.

shuowen:5694.text: A fine man of refinement, spoken of by people. Formed from 彣, with 厂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5695.text: Intersecting strokes. Depicts crossing patterns. All characters in this group are formed from 文.

shuowen:5696.text: Distinctly patterned. Formed from 文, with 非 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “The gentleman changes like a leopard; his pattern is distinct.”

shuowen:5697.text: A mottled pattern. Formed from 文, with 辡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5698.text: Fine strokes. Formed from 文, with 𠩺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5699.text: Long hair flowing, 猋猋. Formed from 長 and 彡. All characters in this group are formed from 髟.

shuowen:5700.text: A root. Formed from 髟, with 犮 indicating the sound.
